comparison: Perfect agreement on background claims (C1-C12). Both evaluations find these established literature-based claims well-supported and treat them as accepted context without challenge.

Perfect agreement on computational methodology (C78-C80). Both evaluations affirm the multiscale simulation approach as valid and well-designed, with peer reviewers explicitly praising the methodology as 'highly compelling.'

Agreement on uncertainty regarding generalizability (C75-C77). Both evaluations recognize these claims as speculative extensions beyond the ELP system. OpenEval notes they require validation in other IDP systems; peer reviewers explicitly cite the limitation to 'very specific architecture' as a weakness.

Strong agreement on FLIM experimental findings (C14-C15, C31-C35). Both evaluations support the fluorescence lifetime measurements demonstrating distinct physicochemical properties. Peer reviewers describe the combined methodology as 'well-designed' without raising concerns about these core experimental results. OpenEval R7 also addresses C36 and C68 not covered in peer R1.

Both support simulation validation claims (C13, C17 in OpenEval R3). Peer R1 broadly affirms the methodology combining simulations and experiments as 'highly compelling.' OpenEval provides more specific detail about the correlation analysis validating the simulation approach.

Agreement on microphase separation findings (C21-C23, C67). Both evaluations support the density distribution analysis showing hydrophobicity-dependent guest block localization. Peer reviewers recognize this as a key contribution to understanding 'micro-structures of coacervates.'

Agreement on structural organization (C24-C26, C70). Both evaluations support the characterization of non-lamellar structures. Peer reviewers affirm the study's success in investigating 'structural organization' and 'higher-resolution structures/substructures.'

Agreement on interpenetrating network structure (C27-C30). Both evaluations support the contact map and radial distribution function analyses. Peer reviewers recognize these findings as valid contributions to understanding condensate micro-structures.

Agreement on interfacial hydrophobicity correlation (C37-C38, C71). Both evaluations support the strong correlation findings. Peer reviewers affirm the study's success in connecting 'sequence to the micro-structure of coacervates.' OpenEval notes potential overstatement in C71's claim that 'a single quantity suffices.'

Agreement on interfacial environment characterization (C39-C42, C16). Both evaluations support the radial distribution function analysis demonstrating interfacial microenvironment. Peer reviewers treat this as part of valid contributions to understanding molecular grammar of phase separation.

Agreement on sequence constraints and frustration (C43-C46, C73-C74). Both evaluations support these findings connecting sequence to structure. Peer reviewers affirm the study's contribution to understanding sequence-structure relationships, though OpenEval notes the concept remains somewhat qualitative.

Agreement on high water content (C47-C48, C69). Both evaluations support the density analysis findings. Peer reviewers recognize this as part of the structural characterization contributing to understanding of condensate micro-structures.

Agreement on hydrogen bonding analysis (C49-C53, C18). Both evaluations support the atomistic simulation findings on hydrogen bond patterns. Peer reviewers affirm the combined theoretical and experimental methodologies without raising concerns about these structural insights.

Agreement on water hydrogen bond density (C54, C56, C58-C59). Both evaluations support the analysis explaining constant per-residue hydrogen bonding. Peer reviewers treat this as part of valid structural characterization of condensate micro-structures.

Agreement on relative solvent accessibility (C60-C62). Both evaluations support the RSA analysis showing intermediate values consistent with interfacial environment. Peer reviewers describe the study as 'well-designed' and accept these structural findings.

Agreement on peptide expansion upon condensation (C63-C66). Both evaluations support the radius of gyration analysis showing counterintuitive expansion. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the structural characterization without challenge.

Both express uncertainty about mean field behavior claims (C72). OpenEval notes potential oversimplification given demonstrated sequence constraints. Peer R6 supports the predictive relationship findings but peer R7 raises concerns about generalizability that relate to the broader applicability of simplified models.

Agreement on optical tweezer mechanical perturbation findings (C36). Both evaluations support the differential response data. OpenEval notes the connection between fluorescence intensity and viscosity could be more rigorously established, while peer reviewers accept the findings without specific concerns.
